title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: David Ellison says AI could be the ‘biggest creative unlock in modern history’
items.content_text: During Paramount Skydance’s latest earnings call, CEO David Ellison likened AI's potential in the film industry to the CGI revolution of the 1990s, labeling it the greatest creative unlock in history. Citing the budget disparity in film production as an example, he argued that AI would drastically optimize output efficiency while maintaining that it serves as a tool for artists rather than a total replacement.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Troubles Leave the AI Industry Reeling
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing scrutiny after reports of an affair with an executive linked to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia’s board has launched an investigation, putting Huang’s position at risk, especially given his status as an at-will employee.

items.title: Here’s what Trump said he knew about Jensen Huang
items.content_text: Donald Trump addressed questions at a White House press briefing regarding when he became aware of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's involvement with an alleged Chinese spy. Intelligence reports suggest the administration was briefed on their relationship over a year ago, yet no action was taken at the time.

items.title: A report by short seller Culper Research from May is resurfacing because it had flagged Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang as "uncomfortably close" (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore's Megaspeed, triggering a formal internal investigation. A short-seller previously flagged their 'uncomfortably close' relationship months ago, while U.S. intelligence officials now suspect she may be an operative recruited to influence chip export controls.

items.title: Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an affair with an executive from an AI compute firm, who has since been identified by intelligence agencies as a foreign spy. Despite Huang's insistence that no proprietary secrets were compromised, the company is under scrutiny due to its central role in global AI hardware supply chains.

items.title: Apple is now offering additional AI access via one-time $50 "intelligence usage packs" when monthly usage caps are met, starting in its Creator Studio apps (Ryan Christoffel/9to5Mac)
items.content_text: Apple has introduced 'intelligence usage packs' in the latest Logic Pro update, charging users $50 once they hit free AI usage limits. This model is expected to roll out to other creative apps, marking the start of Apple’s AI monetization journey.

items.title: Trump says the FBI is "looking into" Jensen Huang's affair, and the Nvidia CEO told him he "had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy" (Associated Press)
items.content_text: Donald Trump claimed that the FBI is investigating an espionage-related matter involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang reportedly defended himself by stating he had no idea the person involved was a spy, as the investigation unfolds.

items.title: Jensen Huang's affair shines a spotlight on Nvidia's weak board and opaque succession planning at what has become the world's most important company (Semafor)
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is mired in scandal following reports of an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, raising serious questions about governance and security. As the architect of Nvidia's dominance, Huang's extreme management style—maintaining over 50 direct reports—has left the company with no clear succession plan and a weak board, exposing the firm to massive operational risks.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead just before its IPO
items.content_text: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 ahead of its IPO, offering significant performance gains and reduced API pricing. The Fable model prioritizes general safety, while Mythos lifts specific restrictions for verified cybersecurity and life sciences organizations.

items.title: AI infrastructure provider Fireworks says hackers accessed some customers' datasets, incomplete model weights, and billing information over the past month (Anna Tong/Forbes)
items.content_text: AI infrastructure provider Fireworks suffered a security breach, allowing hackers to access customers' datasets, partial model weights, and billing info over the past month. Several major clients are already migrating their operations elsewhere.

items.title: SpaceX plans a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, TX, with ~$24B of investment for initial phases, per a public hearing notice (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: SpaceX has submitted a public notice to construct a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, Texas. With an initial investment of approximately $24 billion, the project aims to provide dedicated power and extreme computing performance for aerospace missions.

items.title: Anthropic prices Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at $8/1M input and $40/1M output tokens, down 20% from 5.1; fast mode costs $16/1M input and $80/1M output tokens (Frederic Lardinois/The New Stack)
items.content_text: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, cutting prices by 20% compared to version 5.1. The company also introduced a 'Fast Mode' option, which is priced significantly higher than the standard tier.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, a small AI model built for the repetitive work agents actually do
items.content_text: Meta has launched Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient AI model designed for routine agent tasks like tool calling and document processing. The model prioritizes cost-efficiency, aiming to dominate the AI agent market with a significantly lower price-per-task compared to existing industry rivals.

items.title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
items.content_text: A critical Linux vulnerability dubbed *sshole is currently under active exploitation. The flaw, stemming from the interaction between OpenSSH and the musl library, allows unauthorized root-level access. Threat actors have already begun compromising servers in Southeast Asia and planting backdoors.

items.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
items.content_text: Amid growing public backlash against data centers in the US, Big Tech often frames the issue as a proxy for broader cultural anxieties. However, evidence suggests the root cause is a pragmatic conflict over power grid capacity and the massive electricity demands of AI infrastructure.

items.title: Anthropic says during prerelease testing Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem and solved two open black hole physics problems (Jay Peters/The Verge)
items.content_text: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, featuring enhanced reasoning and coding capabilities. The models have reportedly formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem and solved complex black hole physics problems, aiming to tackle daunting technical challenges with higher efficiency.

items.title: Apple’s $50 Intelligence Usage Packs extend access to some AI features
items.content_text: based AI features. This move marks the first time Apple has monetized specific AI usage within an app to offset costs associated with third-party models from OpenAI and Google.

items.title: Anthropic releases Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2, saying they are "best for the most ambitious, open-ended technical work", for $8/1M input and $40/1M output tokens (Anthropic)
items.content_text: We’ve upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos—models that are designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges. Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. items.title: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
items.content_text: Anthropic has officially launched the Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models, designed to tackle daunting technical challenges. These versions feature significant improvements in coding, logic, and vision with increased speed, reportedly solving complex scientific problems like black hole physics.

items.title: ChatGPT Enterprise now available in AWS Marketplace
items.content_text: OpenAI has made ChatGPT Enterprise available on the AWS Marketplace, allowing organizations to procure the service through existing AWS billing relationships. This move streamlines the procurement process for enterprise clients and accelerates OpenAI's integration into cloud service ecosystems.

items.title: Mavria, which aims to build modular data centers that can be shipped by trucks, raised $130M across pre-seed and seed rounds at a $1B valuation led by Paradigm (Jennifer Hiller/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Mavria has raised $130 million across several rounds, achieving a $1 billion valuation to build modular data centers capable of being transported by truck. The company aims to address the urgent demand for flexible AI infrastructure deployment.

items.title: Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift
items.content_text: Bytedance has introduced the Seedream 5.5 image generation model, tailored for professional workflows. Its key features include stable multi-round editing for up to 100 rounds without color shift and native RGBA transparent background generation, now rolling out across their product suite.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, its smallest and most cost-efficient AI model yet, saying it delivers more intelligence per dollar than Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna (Russell Brandom/TechCrunch)
items.content_text: Meta's Superintelligence Lab has released Muse Ember, a lightweight model optimized for high-frequency agent tasks like tool calls, coding, and document parsing. By offering a significantly lower cost of 10 cents per million input tokens, it challenges competitors like Haiku and Luna to capture the market for large-scale, cost-efficient agentic workflows.

items.title: Instagram’s Effect Builder makes new filters from AI prompts
items.content_text: Instagram has launched the Effect Builder, allowing adult users in the US to create custom filters using text prompts. Users can describe their ideas or upload reference images, with the system optimizing prompts to generate the effects for direct submission.

items.title: The future of AI hinges on… Jensen Huang’s sex life?
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under fire following reports of an affair with former reporter Alice Huang. Her company, Megaspeed, made a sudden, massive $4.8 billion purchase of Nvidia chips, raising alarms as intelligence reports suggest she acted as a honeypot for China’s MSS to gain access to sensitive commercial and potentially political communication.

items.title: Uber launches Uber Parking, an in-app parking reservation tool powered by its SpotHero acquisition, in 15 US cities, including Chicago, NYC, and San Francisco (Andrew J. Hawkins/The Verge)
items.content_text: Uber has integrated SpotHero technology to launch an in-app parking reservation tool across 15 US cities. The feature allows users to search, book, and pay for parking spots, utilizing QR codes or license plate recognition to manage the parking experience directly within the Uber ecosystem.

items.title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
items.content_text: California State Senator Scott Wiener, having won the congressional seat vacated by Nancy Pelosi, has prioritized AI regulation. Citing new reports on recursive self-improvement in AI, he criticized Congress for its slow pace and demanded urgent federal legislation to mitigate existential risks.

items.title: French officials say Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind the cyberattacks that knocked out commercial refrigerators and freezers across France in October (Reuters)
items.content_text: French officials have accused the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyberattacks in October that disabled commercial refrigerators and freezers across France. These attacks disrupted retail cold chains, sparking significant concerns regarding the vulnerability of critical national infrastructure.

items.title: Disney bets on Adobe's Firefly to create brand-safe AI models for its entertainment empire
items.content_text: Disney announced a multi-year partnership with Adobe at the MAX conference, utilizing Adobe's Firefly Foundry to train custom AI models embedded with its core IP. Driven by divisions like Imagineering and ESPN Edge, the project aims to integrate production-ready, brand-safe generative tools into theme park development, film production, and sports content creation.

items.title: Sources: a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China was transferred to the DOJ after Nvidia intervened (New York Times)
items.content_text: Singapore-based Megaspeed is under fire for allegedly smuggling Nvidia's high-end A-series chips into China. Following Nvidia's intervention and cooperation, the Commerce Department has escalated the case to the Department of Justice, signaling a shift from administrative probe to criminal investigation.
